subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender durable agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, lifecycle/quota, memory, skill, and config boundaries become the public contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior crosses channel routing, durable agent creation, memory isolation, per-agent skills/config, resource lifecycle, and security boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Design a generic identity-to-agent contract first
options.body: Create an opt-in, admin-authorized lifecycle and memory contract that Feishu can implement without hidden Feishu-only policy.

options.title: Keep session scoping plus explicit subagents
options.body: Continue using group_sender or group_topic_sender session scoping, static bindings, and explicit thread-bound sessions_spawn until a broader contract is approved.

options.title: Defer to external deployments or plugins
options.body: Leave automatic provisioning to deployment-specific plugins unless maintainers identify a missing OpenClaw channel or agent API seam.

recommendation.title: Design a generic identity-to-agent contract first
recommendation.body: Create an opt-in, admin-authorized lifecycle and memory contract that Feishu can implement without hidden Feishu-only policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The requested behavior starts in the Feishu channel/plugin boundary, and the package metadata identifies m1heng as the Feishu plugin community contact.
